findings.title: plot.ipynb 'Coloring by hue' (cell 26) and 'Adding a legend' (cell 29) crash on fresh execution: hue length 8120 != 8124 rows
findings.description: The primary plotting tutorial builds its hue vector as split=int(mushrooms.shape[0]/5) then hue=[1]*split+['two']*split+[3.0]*split+[None]*split+['four']*split. mushrooms has 8124 rows and 8124/5 is not integer: int(8124/5)=1624, so 5*1624=8120 labels -- 4 short of 8124. The QC-2026-07 hue-length hardening (hypertools/plot/plot.py:2006-2010) now raises ValueError for any hue whose length != n_obs, so BOTH cell 26 and cell 29 raise. In a real top-to-bottom 'Run All' (Colab/Jupyter), execution stops at cell 26 and every subsequent section (labels, clustering, normalization, alignment, text) never runs. The committed notebook still shows rendered figures for these cells, so the committed outputs are STALE and unreproducible. The error message itself is good (names problem + fix); the defect is the tutorial code's off-by-remainder arithmetic. Control test: rebuilding hue to length 8124 (assigning the remainder to the last group) makes hyp.plot(...,hue=...,legend=True) succeed, confirming the arithmetic is the sole cause.
findings.expected: Tutorial cell colors the mushrooms scatter into 5 equal groups and renders a figure (as the committed output depicts).
findings.actual: ValueError: hue has 8120 entries but the data has 8124 observations; hue must have exactly one value (or one row, for a matrix hue) per observation.

findings.title: analyze.ipynb states weights elements are '(300,100)' / '300 TRs' but actual (and committed) shape is (100,100)
findings.description: analyze.ipynb cell 6 code carries the inline comment '# 300 TRs and 100 components' and the following markdown (cell 7) says 'We can see that the elements of weights each have the dimensions (300,100).' hyp.load('weights_avg') actually returns two (100,100) arrays; the cell's own committed stream output is '(100, 100)\n(100, 100)', and the freshly-executed heatmap is unmistakably 100x100. The prose is internally contradicted by the notebook's own output. Prose should read (100,100)/100 timepoints. (Note: the FULL weights dataset used by align.ipynb is 36 arrays of (300,100); the '300' figure appears to have been carried over from that dataset.)
findings.expected: Comment/markdown match the data and committed output: elements are (100,100).
findings.actual: cell 6 comment '# 300 TRs and 100 components'; cell 7 markdown 'each have the dimensions (300,100)'; actual/committed shape (100, 100).

findings.title: align.ipynb describes its dataset as 'a list of 2 numpy arrays ... from 18 subjects' but hyp.load('weights') returns 36 arrays of (300,100)
findings.description: align.ipynb cell 6 markdown says: 'This dataset is a list of 2 numpy arrays, each containing average brain activity (fMRI) from 18 subjects ... The rows are timepoints and the columns are fMRI components.' But cell 7 loads data = hyp.load('weights') -- the FULL weights dataset, which is a list of 36 arrays each (300,100), not 2 arrays. The description was copied verbatim from the weights_avg tutorials (reduce/analyze) and is factually wrong for this notebook. Cell 9 markdown further says 'the first hundred data points from two arrays', whereas cell 10 actually averages 36 arrays into two groups. Users reading the description will mis-model the data.
findings.expected: Description matches loaded data: 36 subject arrays of shape (300,100).
findings.actual: markdown: 'a list of 2 numpy arrays, each ... from 18 subjects'; actual: 36 arrays of (300,100).

findings.title: plot.ipynb text section claims to load 'all State of the Union Addresses from 1989-2017' but the code uses 4 hard-coded sample sentences
findings.description: plot.ipynb cell 48 markdown: "we'll load in an example text dataset to get started which is comprised of all State of the Union Addresses from 1989-2017." The immediately following cell 49 does NOT load any SOTU corpus; it defines sample_sotus_speeches, a Python list of exactly 4 hard-coded demo sentences (with the comment 'Create sample State of the Union text data for demonstration'). Cell 50 markdown continues 'Simply pass the list of text data to the plot function'. The tutorial appears to have been trimmed to avoid downloading the large sotus dataset, but the surrounding prose still promises the full corpus, overstating what the example does. The resulting figure is a single short trajectory, not the rich SOTU trajectory the prose implies.
findings.repro: grep -n 'all State of the Union' docs/tutorials/plot.ipynb ; grep -n 'sample_sotus_speeches' docs/tutorials/plot.ipynb
findings.expected: Prose matches code -- either load the real sotus dataset, or reword to say 'a few example sentences'.
findings.actual: markdown promises 'all State of the Union Addresses from 1989-2017'; code defines a 4-element list of demo sentences.

findings.title: Tutorials teach the deprecated reduce syntax {'model':...,'params':{...}}; reduce.ipynb emits a fresh DeprecationWarning (plot/analyze silently swallow it)
findings.description: reduce.ipynb (cells 24-25), analyze.ipynb (cells 20-21) and plot.ipynb (cells 22-23) all demonstrate finer parameter control via reduce={'model':'PCA','params':{'whiten':True}}. On fresh execution this now emits DeprecationWarning: "{'model': ..., 'params': {...}} is deprecated; use {'model': ..., 'args': [...], 'kwargs': {...}} instead". The committed reduce cell 25 has no such warning, so the committed output is stale. The tutorials therefore teach a deprecated API that will presumably be removed. Secondary inconsistency: the warning fires for the direct hyp.reduce(...) call (reduce cell 25) but NOT for hyp.plot(..., reduce={...'params'...}) (plot cell 23) nor hyp.analyze(..., reduce={...'params'...}) (analyze cell 21) -- the plot/analyze dispatch paths swallow the deprecation, so users get inconsistent signals about the same deprecated dict.
findings.repro: cd /Users/jmanning/hypertools && MPLBACKEND=Agg .venv/bin/python -W always -c "import hypertools as hyp;w=hyp.load('weights_avg');hyp.reduce(w, reduce={'model':'PCA','params':{'whiten':True}}, ndims=3)" 2>&1 | grep -i deprecat
findings.expected: Tutorials use the current, non-deprecated reduce parameter syntax (model + kwargs), and all three entry points (reduce/plot/analyze) agree on whether 'params' is deprecated.
findings.actual: DeprecationWarning: {'model': ..., 'params': {...}} is deprecated; use {'model': ..., 'args': [...], 'kwargs': {...}} instead  (fires only via hyp.reduce; plot/analyze emit nothing)

findings.title: align.ipynb group split drops subject index 17 (np.mean(data[:17]) + np.mean(data[18:]) over 36 subjects)
findings.description: align.ipynb cell 10 (and the analogous cells 13/16) splits the 36-subject weights data into two groups with group1=np.mean(data[:17],0) and group2=np.mean(data[18:],0). data[:17] is subjects 0-16 (17 subjects) and data[18:] is subjects 18-35 (18 subjects); the subject at index 17 is silently excluded from both groups. This is an off-by-one: to split 36 subjects into two equal halves the code should be data[:18] and data[18:]. It does not crash and the demonstration still 'works', but it is a latent bug in tutorial code that users are likely to copy, and it drops a data point without comment.
findings.repro: cd /Users/jmanning/hypertools && .venv/bin/python -c "import hypertools as hyp;d=hyp.load('weights');print('n=',len(d),'group1 uses',len(d[:17]),'group2 uses',len(d[18:]),'-> index 17 dropped')"
findings.expected: Both groups together cover all 36 subjects (e.g. data[:18] and data[18:]).
findings.actual: group1 uses 17 subjects (0-16), group2 uses 18 (18-35); subject index 17 excluded.

findings.title: Inconsistent 'supported models' lists: UMAP listed in reduce cell 2 & plot cell 19 but omitted in reduce cell 24 & analyze cell 15 (UMAP is supported)
findings.description: The enumerations of supported dimensionality-reduction models disagree across tutorials. reduce.ipynb cell 2 ends '...MDS and UMAP' and plot.ipynb cell 19 ends '...MDS, UMAP' (UMAP included), but reduce.ipynb cell 24 and analyze.ipynb cell 15 end '...LocallyLinearEmbedding, and MDS' (UMAP omitted). UMAP is in fact supported (hyp.reduce(weights, reduce='UMAP', ndims=3) returns (100,3) for both arrays with umap-learn 0.5.11 installed), so the shorter lists are wrong/incomplete. Pick one canonical list.
findings.expected: All supported-model lists match and include UMAP (or consistently exclude it if unsupported).
findings.actual: reduce cell2/plot cell19 include UMAP; reduce cell24/analyze cell15 omit it; UMAP works.
